newsitem.title: UK: Dollar propped in late Europe by robust U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Dollar propped in late Europe by robust U.S. data.

text.p: The dollar was firm in late European trade, supported by renewed prospect of higher U.S. interest rates after robust U.S. consumer confidence data.
The U.S. Conference Board said its May consumer confidence index hit a 28-year peak to 127.1 against an upwardly revised 118.5 for April and well above analysts' expectations of 114.4.

"This is not normally a key figure for the market but at this stage of the economic cycle, this rise is more significant," said Thomas Rayner, international economist at Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull. "It's an indication the Fed will need to do something."

The dollar's gains contrasted with U.S. bonds extending their earlier losses after the data and a slip in the Dow Jones Industrials stock index. This highlighted the market's perception of the prospect of higher U.S. rates, said dealers.
By 1520 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.6982/92 marks, down from a session high of 1.7015 and above late Monday's European level of 1.6897/02 marks.
Against the yen, the dollar stood at 116.38/43 from 116.65 earlier and 116.44/49 Wednesday.
The dollar was also seen supported by uncertainty in Europe monetary union project following French elections Sunday.

France's opposition Socialists' lead over the ruling centre-right in the first round vote is seen as raising the chances of a broad-based EMU start and the prospect of a weaker euro. The run-off vote will be held on June 1.
"We could see some liberal interpretation (from France's Socialists) of the EMU criteria which points to a weaker euro," said a U.S. bank dealer. "The safest place to be is going to be the dollar."
The traditional safe-haven Swiss franc weakened today despite the EMU uncertainty, after Swiss National Bank senior officials said they were unhappy with recent franc strength.

SNB president Hans Meyer said earlier today he was not content with the recent strengthening of the franc. This was echoed by SNB vice chairman Jean-Pierre Roth who also said the central bank was not ruling out lower interest rates, referring to money market interest rates.
SNB has been adding liquidity to the money markets more aggressively since last week in a bid to stem franc strength.
Dollar/Swiss franc was trading at 1.4167/72, down from a session high of 1.4192 but up from Monday's 1.4021/31.
Mark/Swiss franc was also firmer at 83.30/32 centimes against 82.92/95 Monday.
Dealers said the sell-off in Czech crown today after the floating of the crown late Monday was also dollar supportive.
The Czech central bank eliminated the crown's fluctuation band against a mark/dollar basket, pushing the crown down around eight percent on the dollar and seven percent against the mark.
The central bank had intervened on several occasions over the past 10 days and hiked interest rates to stem speculative attacks against the currency.
Dollar/crown stood at 32.969/149, down from the 33.467 high and well above levels around 30.25 late Monday.
